description:
Every event the SDK tracks today goes to Amplitude, because the event engine has no concept of a destination. EventTracker is defined on both platforms as a protocol that abstracts Amplitude event tracking, and neither MartechKit nor MartechPack contains any notion of a destination, of routing, or of a destination being forbidden. Amplitude is not the default. It is the only thing the engine can express.

That assumption is already wrong in production. rs_ad_revenue must reach AppsFlyer and must never reach Amplitude or Firebase, so it shipped in MartechKit 2.0 as a hardcoded exception instead of a rule. MT-1556 is currently applying that same contract by hand across seven apps in the portfolio, one release at a time. That manual rollout is what it costs, every time, for the SDK to be unable to say where an event goes.

Martech confirmed on 7 July that this is not a one-off. Destinations are per-event, the set can differ per event, and some destinations are explicitly forbidden for an event. The agreed model is a closed set of destinations (Amplitude, AppsFlyer, Firebase), declared per event in the martech-guidelines schemas, generated into both SDKs, with no routing decisions in app code.

This epic gives an event an explicit set of destinations, so that a rule replaces the exception and a new destination requirement becomes a schema change rather than a hand rollout across the portfolio.

This depends on the martech-guidelines schemas carrying destination and forbidden-destination fields. That work sits with Martech and is not tracked on this board.

Acceptance criteria:
- An event declares which destinations it reaches, and the SDK delivers it to those and to no others
- A destination that is forbidden for an event is provably not reached, and is caught before release rather than in BigQuery afterwards
- rs_ad_revenue is expressed as a rule rather than a hardcoded exception, with no behaviour change for apps already on 2.0
- Destination rules come from the martech-guidelines schemas, and no routing decision lives in app code
- Adding a destination to an event is a schema change and a regenerate, not a code change in every app
- Works on both iOS and Android
